title: Signing in works
how: Go to the platform address. Type your email and password. Click the sign-in button.
expected: You land on the Portfolio page, and your name shows at the top right.
comment: A pretty straight forward username and password tab that's familiar to all platforms.

title: A wrong password is refused
how: Sign out. Try to sign in with the right email and a wrong password.
expected: You stay on the sign-in page and it says the email and password do not match an account. Nothing else is shown.

title: Signing out works
how: Click your name at the top right, then sign out.
expected: You are returned to the sign-in page.

title: A signed-out person sees nothing
how: While signed out, paste a project link into the address bar and press Enter.
expected: You are sent to the sign-in page. No project information is shown first.

title: Every menu item opens
how: Click each item in the left menu in turn: Overview, Portfolio, Projects, Process model, Policies, Contacts, Settings.
expected: Each one opens its own page. Nothing shows an error page or a blank screen.

title: The menu can be narrowed
how: Click the collapse arrow at the bottom of the left menu, then refresh the page.
expected: The menu shrinks to icons only, and it is still shrunk after the refresh.

title: Unfinished items are honest
how: Hover over the greyed-out menu items — Approvals, Benchmarks, Reports.
expected: Each one says “Not built yet” and cannot be clicked. Nothing pretends to work.

title: Search finds things quickly
how: Press Ctrl+K. Type part of a project name. Press Enter on a result.
expected: A search box opens, matching projects and steps are listed, and Enter opens the one chosen.

title: A project can be created
how: Projects → Add project. Fill in the name, code and client, and work through the three steps.
expected: The project is created and opens, and it is listed on the Projects page with its code and client.

title: The project menu appears
how: Open the project.
expected: The left menu now shows this project’s steps, grouped by stage — Set up, Cost planning, Measurement, and so on.

title: Project details can be changed
how: In the project menu open Project Details. Change the client name and click Save changes.
expected: The change is saved, and the new client name shows on the project.

title: A project can be archived
how: On Project Details click Archive, then go back to Projects.
expected: The project leaves the working list and is shown as archived. It is not deleted.
comment: It did archive but once it's archived the project is hard to find. There's no clear "Archived" label almost as though it was deleted. I can't search for the project either. No trace

title: An empty project says so
how: Open a brand-new project and go to Project Corpus.
expected: It says there are no documents filed yet, and offers the way to import them.
comment: Doesn't mention the word "empty" but it's easy to assume it's empty and it does give you a way to import the documents

title: Documents can be imported
how: Import a folder of the project’s documents.
expected: Every file is listed with the kind it was recognised as, and the import finishes without errors.

title: Unknown files are asked about, not guessed
how: Include one file with an unclear name in the import.
expected: That file is listed as still needing a kind, and asks you what it is instead of choosing for you.
comment: asked me what kind of file it was

title: Documents reach the right steps
how: After importing, open two or three steps in the project menu.
expected: Each step lists the documents it needs, and the ones you filed are shown against them.

title: The original can be opened
how: In Project Corpus, click a document’s name.
expected: The original document opens in a new tab and is readable. The page behind it is not lost.

title: A document can be withdrawn
how: In Project Corpus, withdraw one document, then open the step that used it.
expected: It is gone from the corpus, and the step now says that document is missing.

title: A step will not run without its documents
how: Open a step whose documents have not been filed.
expected: The run button is greyed out, and the page names exactly which documents are missing.

title: Filing what is missing releases it
how: File the documents it named, then return to the step.
expected: The run button is now available.

title: The step reads the documents
how: Click the button that starts the step — for example “Extract the estimate inputs” — and wait for it to finish.
expected: Figures appear one by one, and each one shows the document it came from.

title: Every figure can be traced
how: Click the source shown next to a figure.
expected: The exact wording from the document is shown.

title: Nothing is invented
how: Look for a figure the documents do not state.
expected: It says “Not stated” instead of showing a number.

title: Your own figure wins
how: Type your own figure over one the step proposed, click elsewhere on the page, then refresh.
expected: Your figure is saved without pressing a save button, is marked as yours, and is still there after the refresh.

title: An incomplete step cannot be signed
how: Leave one required figure empty and try to sign off.
expected: Sign-off is refused, and it names the figure that is missing.

title: A complete step can be signed
how: Fill in every required figure, then sign off.
expected: The step shows “Signed off”, with your name and the date — for example 12 Aug 2026.

title: Signed figures are frozen
how: Try to change a figure on the step you have just signed.
expected: The change is refused. Signed figures cannot be edited.

title: The next step is released
how: Before signing, open the step that follows — for example Cost Plan. Then sign the earlier step and open it again.
expected: Before: it says it is waiting on the earlier step. After: it can be started, and it carries the signed figures through.

title: A bill can be drafted
how: Open Bill of Quantities and run it.
expected: Rows are produced, each with a description, a unit and a quantity.

title: Pricing shows the same bill
how: Open Pricing.
expected: The same rows are shown, and it states how many are still unpriced.

title: A rate works out correctly
how: Type a rate on one row.
expected: The amount equals the rate times the quantity, and the total at the bottom goes up by that amount.

title: Many rows can be priced at once
how: Tick several rows, then apply a rate or a percentage to the selection.
expected: Only the ticked rows change, and by the figure that was typed.

title: Nothing is shown before it is signed
how: Open Portfolio while the project has nothing signed off.
expected: No invented figures. Each empty tile names the step that would supply it, and links to that step.

title: Signed figures appear
how: Open the project’s Dashboard after signing a step.
expected: The figures shown are the ones that were signed, and nothing else.

title: The report can be issued
how: Open the project’s report and download the PDF.
expected: The PDF downloads, opens, and its figures match what is on the screen.

title: Money and dates read correctly
how: Look at any money figure and any date on screen.
expected: Money reads R 1 234 567,89 — rand, spaces, comma. Dates read 12 Aug 2026, never 08/12/26.

title: A contact can be added
how: Contacts → add an organisation, with the person who answers there.
expected: It is saved and shown under the right kind — client, supplier, and so on.

title: A duplicate is refused politely
how: Add the same organisation a second time under the same kind.
expected: It is refused with a plain message explaining why — not a technical error.

title: Firm figures can be changed
how: Settings → change one figure and save it.
expected: It saves, and the row now names you as the person who set it.

title: A wrong figure is refused
how: Settings → enter a figure with the decimal in the wrong place, for example 950 instead of 9,5.
expected: It is refused with a message, and the old figure stays.

title: Reference pages open
how: Open Policies, then Process model.
expected: Both open and can be read.

title: It fits the screen
how: Work through three or four pages on a normal laptop screen.
expected: Nothing overlaps, nothing is cut off, and there is no sideways scrolling.

title: Nothing shows a raw error
how: Through the whole test, watch for anything that looks technical.
expected: No error codes, no stack traces, no blank white pages at any point.
